## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] NINDS describes Parkinson’s disease as a progressive nervous-system disorder involving nerve-cell damage and death; WHO also describes worsening over time. (medium confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease
- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation distinguishes parkinsonism, a set of movement symptoms, from a specific diagnosis; the MDS criteria separately assess whether Parkinson’s disease is its cause. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/what-is-parkinsons/types-parkinsonisms · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/
- [statement] For determining Parkinson’s disease as the cause of parkinsonism, the MDS criteria use absolute exclusions, red flags counterbalanced by supportive criteria, and supportive features. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/ · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape
- [statement] The MDS criteria distinguish clinically established Parkinson’s disease, prioritizing specificity, from probable disease, balancing sensitivity and specificity. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/ · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape
- [statement] WHO and NINDS describe non-motor involvement in Parkinson’s disease, including mental-health and sleep problems. (medium confidence) — https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease, https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease
- [statement] NINDS notes that some people with Parkinson’s disease never develop tremor. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape
- [statement] NINDS states that no specific single test can definitively diagnose Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape
- [statement] NINDS states that a dopamine transporter scan cannot distinguish Parkinson’s disease from atypical parkinsonism; Beach and Adler likewise describe dopamine functional scans as lacking specificity for Parkinson’s disease. (medium confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6544441/
- [statement] WHO reported that global estimates for 2019 showed over 8.5 million individuals with Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-08-09) — https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/parkinson-disease · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Beach and Adler report that autopsy-validated studies found misdiagnosis common in early clinically diagnosed Parkinson’s disease compared with patients followed for years. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6544441/ · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The MDS clinical diagnostic criteria define motor parkinsonism as bradykinesia plus rest tremor or rigidity. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26474316/ · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape

## Research summary — Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape

Parkinson’s disease is a progressive nervous-system disorder with movement and non-motor manifestations. Parkinsonism describes a movement syndrome rather than a specific diagnosis, and secondary causes broaden its differential diagnosis. The MDS clinical criteria formalize syndrome recognition and assessment of Parkinson’s disease as its cause. Clinical uncertainty, including the limitations of dopamine imaging and early diagnosis, remains central to interpreting the landscape. WHO also documents a substantial global burden and unequal access to care.
